mappings.note: One marble from five equally likely. Simple event, LO-3.
Vowels among the 11 letters of PROBABILITY, single draw. Simple event, LO-3.
One die, 'at most 2' meaning faces 1 and 2. Simple event, LO-3; one die is not a compound experiment.
Applies P(not E) = 1 - P(E) to a given probability. Complement rule only, LO-4; no sample space is counted, so LO-3 does not fit.
A lemon-only bag makes an orange candy impossible, so P = 0. The point is the lower bound of the probability range, LO-2, not a favourable count.
'Not defective' is the complement of the 12 defective bulbs. Complement outcome, LO-4.
'Neither red nor a queen' is the complement of a union, needing care not to double-count the two red queens. The clearest complement-of-a-compound-event item in the chapter, LO-4.
Consonants among 26 letters. The event is stated positively and the count is a direct 26 - 5, so LO-3 rather than the complement outcome LO-4.
Perfect squares among cards 3 to 50; the only subtlety is that n(S) = 48, not 50. Simple event, LO-3.
'Multiple of 3 or 7' over 20 tickets, handled by pooling favourable numbers with no overlap. A single draw, so LO-3; LO-4's compound events are cards, dice and coins.

The whole difficulty is realising the sample space is the 7 possible leftover weekdays, not the 365 days: that is C-8.1-LO-4 (lists the sample space of a random experiment). LO-3 then covers the routine 1/7.
Two dice, product 6, over the 36-pair space. Compound dice event, LO-4.
Spinner with 8 equally likely sectors, factors of 8 favourable. Simple event, LO-3.
Divisible by both 2 and 3, i.e. by 6, among 25 cards. Single draw with a conjunctive condition, LO-3.
Primes among 1 to 30. Simple event, LO-3.
Primes below 23 among 90 discs, so the favourable count is bounded by 23 while n(S) stays 90. Simple event, LO-3.

Requires the mean of the ten listed values (7) before any probability can be found, so it reaches into the central-tendency competency C-8.1 as well as the simple-event LO-3. C-8.1's wording says 'grouped frequency distributions' and this list is ungrouped, which is the closest available fit.
One die, prime face. Simple event, LO-3.
'Odd or less than 4' on one die, resolved by pooling {1,2,3,5} without double-counting. Single die, so a simple event, LO-3.
Two dice, sum 9, four favourable ordered pairs out of 36. Compound dice event, LO-4.
Rejects 1.1 as a probability. Pure range statement, LO-2.
'Not red' is the complement of the red balls. Complement outcome, LO-4, even though the answer counts the blacks directly.
Three coins, exactly two heads, over the eight-outcome space. The largest coin sample space in the chapter and squarely a compound coin event, LO-4.
|x| < 3 over nine listed numbers. Single draw, LO-3.
Even prime on a die, i.e. only the face 2. Simple event, LO-3.
